Use this sheet with [the exercise](exercise-student.html). Predict before reading the results, then explain in words. These figures use exact updating or supplied fits, with no new Stan inference.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(here)
source(here("R/functions.R"))
source(here("R/course_data.R"))
source(here("R/course_utils.R"))
source(here("R/course_visuals.R"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,fig.width=8,fig.height=4.5)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=14))
```

## The core comparison: mother trees

```{r core-results}
fit <- course_fit("day3_trees")
trees <- make_tree_data()
knitr::kable(trees |> select(tree,n,suv) |> mutate(observed=suv/n),digits=3)
comparison <- mother_comparison(fit,seed=20261024)
plot_mother_comparison(comparison)
plot_mother_movement(comparison)
knitr::kable(comparison |> select(tree,n,model,mean,lower,upper),digits=3)
```

The complete and separate models use flat Beta(1,1) priors on the probabilities.
The partial model uses a shared Normal distribution on the logit scale, with its
centre and SD estimated. Prior formulations also differ in this comparison.
Movement depends on group information and the inferred differences among trees.
It does not guarantee smaller error for every tree.

## Instructor demonstrations and research connections

```{r demonstrations}
plot_group_spread()
knitr::kable(course_diagnostics(fit),digits=2)
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(fit$draws,pars=c("mu","sigma"))
plot_mother_check(fit)
plot_cndd_species()
plot_cndd_abundance()
plot_wood_density()
```

CNDD species curves and the abundance relationship are conceptual simulations.
The wood-density plot uses a saved fit to simulated allometry data. Neither is
an empirical result from the cited research. The shared structure is an individual
model plus group differences. The response distribution changes between examples.
